title: Choose Virtue
coreMove: Stillness needs a moral aim: put goodness before ease, applause, and appetite, so your calm makes you more honest, useful, brave, restrained, and just.

exampleSpecs.audience: Mederic drafting an internal decision memo
exampleSpecs.stakes: a restricted gift could fund beds while excluding the hardest guests
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The written memo refuses a donor condition that would make service cleaner but less just.

exampleSpecs.audience: Edmund and Carter handling the same staff shortage
exampleSpecs.stakes: public image could outrun the duty to serve the oldest residents first
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Edmund protects image while Carter uses the imperial duty standard to serve the common good.

exampleSpecs.audience: Maelle freezing before a hard hospitality task
exampleSpecs.stakes: private calm could become distance from the people at the door
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Bruno gives a quotable reframe that sends Maelle back into service.

exampleSpecs.audience: Odilon learning how virtue guides calm
exampleSpecs.stakes: a learner could treat calm as the answer instead of testing the act
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The learner's confusion becomes a four-column test of courage, justice, temperance, and wisdom.

exampleSpecs.audience: Vivian changing the order of her morning replies
exampleSpecs.stakes: pleasant praise could keep urgent repair work out of sight
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The same inbox routine is shown before and after the goodness-first change.

exampleSpecs.audience: service leaders checking whether order still serves people
exampleSpecs.stakes: a smooth process may quietly reward applause over justice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The useful mark is a small absence in service paperwork that exposes moral drift.
